title: Static Wide-Disc Ray
description: One original stylised ray-inspired animal exterior. The thick low central body, rounded forward snout and broad flattened pectoral disc form one continuous closed surface, with gently raised finite-thickness lateral fin margins and receding concave rear edges. The body tapers directly into one long narrow gently sideways-curving tail; two small dark eyes are partly seated on the dorsal front body. All body/disc section geometry, tail trajectory and eye placements are newly authored, not a kite given eyes, a bat with its skeleton removed, a recoloured tadpole, a widened fish skeleton or separately overlapped wing plates. Generic connected-mesh orientation, ear clipping, small eye ellipsoid and mature export/render infrastructure are reused only. One whole body/disc/tail mesh plus two closed small eyes; three opaque untextured matte PBR materials. One prop, zero scenes. Metres, native Z up, head/front -Y, full horizontal bounds-centred ground origin, finite flat central belly underside in a fixed display rest. Artistic static exterior only, not a real species identification, anatomical specimen, internal skeleton, functioning gill/respiratory structure, swimming or fluid simulation, rig, animation, biological fidelity, buoyancy or ecological performance. No venom, sting or safety capability is represented.
